question.text: Per the chapter, which definition of poverty is attributed to Nobel Laureate Amartya Sen and referenced alongside the UN's multidimensional definition?

answer.text: 'Poverty is the mathematical shortfall of household income below Rs 27/day urban'
'Poverty is not just absence of income. Poverty is presence of Helplessness, Powerlessness and Voicelessness.'
'Poverty is purely a function of low-productivity agriculture in aspirational districts'

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.5.1 (i), Amartya Sen's definition is: 'Poverty is not just absence of income. Poverty is presence of Helplessness, Powerlessness and Voicelessness.' This aligns with the UN's multidimensional definition. The Trap: Option A is a Tendulkar-committee-style quantitative poverty line — not Sen. Option C reduces poverty to agricultural productivity. Option D equates poverty with unemployment. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to Ch 4 (Logic Model) and Ch 6 (Frameworks). SIAs use these conceptual anchors when drafting SAS-1300 financial inclusion and poverty-alleviation assurance statements. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When designing beneficiary questionnaires for SAS-1300 engagements, include agency/voice indicators (Likert scale on decision-making power, freedom-of-choice items) — not just income metrics. Sen's framing is a practical reminder to measure capability, not just income deltas.
